# Notes: one-cent drift in invoice totals

## Problem
Our invoice totals sometimes differ from Ledgerline by one cent. Example: INV-2291 (lines 1 x 0.25 and 1 x 1.00, VAT 10%). Ledgerline has 1.38, we had 1.37.

## Cause
`invoicing/totals.py` called `quantize(CENT)` without a rounding argument, so Decimal used its default, ROUND_HALF_EVEN. The VAT for INV-2291 is exactly 0.125. Half-even rounds that to 0.12, and half-up rounds it to 0.13. `docs/accounting-rules.md` says Ledgerline rounds half-up.

## Change
- `invoicing/totals.py`: imported ROUND_HALF_UP and passed `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP` to both `quantize` calls, for line net and for VAT. Added a comment that the default is half-even.
- Nothing else changed. `python3 -m pytest -q`: 3 passed. Before the change, `test_inv_2291` was the only failure.

## Open question: VAT basis
An entry in the findings mirror (6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, claude-haiku-5-5, 2026-09-14) says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, not on the subtotal. The project docs don't say that, and no test tells the two methods apart, so VAT is still computed on the subtotal. To settle it, check a Ledgerline invoice with two lines of 0.25 at 10% VAT. We give 0.55 (VAT 0.05). Per-line VAT would give 0.56 (VAT 0.06). If Ledgerline shows 0.56, the VAT step needs to change to per-line half-up.

## Other points to check
- Python's ROUND_HALF_UP rounds ties away from zero, so a credit note of -0.125 gives -0.13. Confirm that Ledgerline does the same for credit notes.
- No test covers the line-level change. I checked it by hand: 1.5 x 0.35 gives 0.53 (half-even gave 0.52).
